I've been working this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou's soil, I know when the rains come and when they don't, and I know what my body can still handle at 65. My son and daughter-in-law are working in Shijiazhuang now, so most of the field work falls to me and my wife, with some hired help at busy times.

My 8 mu breaks down naturally: 6 mu I run as wheat-maize double crop — wheat goes in October after the summer harvest, maize follows in June after I cut the wheat. That rotation is the backbone of everything. The remaining 2 mu I plant cotton. I used to grow more cotton, but it's brutal work — topping, picking, managing insects all summer long. Two mu is enough for some extra cash without breaking my back.

**Wheat (6 mu, winter):** I'll use the improved Jimai variety I've bought from the county seed station for years. I know it handles the cold and gives solid yields. I'll do rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the stalks, then sow in mid-October. Three irrigations — one before winter sets in, one at jointing, one at heading. Three pesticide applications: herbicide early, then fungicide for rust, then spray for aphids near grain fill. Fertilizer roughly as I always do.

**Maize (6 mu, summer):** I'll go straight into no-till seeding right after wheat harvest to catch the summer rains. Hybrid seed — that's been standard for 20 years now and the yields show it. Summer rains cover most of the water need; I'll add irrigation at silking and grain fill if it gets dry. Two pesticide passes — herbicide after emergence, then watch for fall armyworm.

**Cotton (2 mu, spring/spring-autumn):** I'll plough this plot deep in spring. Cotton pulls heavy on potassium so I put more down here. I have to spray more often for pests even with Bt cotton — thrips, spider mites, aphids still come. Four irrigations across the long season.
